correlationContract: D7 — deriveCorrelationNonce({chainId, tokenAddress, payerAddress, dispatchId: the action-digest string, seed: hex-decoded grant.nonce})
note: Generated, committed and drift-gated (the runner re-derives this corpus in memory and diffs). Keys are FIXED test-only seeds; their private halves are effectively public and must never be reused. Exactly ONE vector has expect=ACCEPT; controls that share the positive code assert the code, not acceptance.

vectors.name: valid-reconfirmed
vectors.description: R-18..R-22, B1-B6 all green: CALLDATA route, depth >= minConfirmations, txStatus SUCCESS, ENFORCED hold, independent observer kid.

vectors.name: reject-correlation-mismatch
vectors.description: §9.5 — the correlation mutated by one byte; recomputation from the bundle's own receipt+grant disagrees.

vectors.name: reject-sibling-seed
vectors.description: REVISION 3 — same grant, DIFFERENT seed; the sibling nonce settles on-chain for real, and recomputation from grant.nonce still yields THE one nonce. The D7 seed-pin knockout vector.

vectors.name: reject-digest-over-other-grant
vectors.description: A genuine settlement of mandate D filed as evidence for the base mandate: both reference hashes point at the base bundle, correlation carries D's on-chain value. Recomputation refuses. Knockout: accept a supplied correlation instead of recomputing -> GREEN.

vectors.name: reject-cross-tenant-correlation
vectors.description: §9.2 — tenant A's on-chain value re-filed under tenant B's bundle and tenant field; the digest recomputed over tenant B's receipt derives different bytes.

vectors.name: reject-grant-extra-member
vectors.description: R-12's inherited closed-world refusal: a grant carrying a twelfth member would let two honest parties compute two different digests.

vectors.name: reject-grant-multi-use
vectors.description: R-12's inherited single-use refusal: maxUses != 1 is not the grant the digest binds.

vectors.name: reject-tenantless-receipt
vectors.description: R-AD-6 — a schema-conformant receipt with scope.tenant absent produces NO digest; the narrowing is a vector, not a runtime surprise.

vectors.name: reject-cross-tenant-field
vectors.description: R-11 — the artifact's own tenant does not equal the verifier's expected value; caught offline with no chain access.

vectors.name: reject-retry-replay
vectors.description: §9.3 — retry #1's settlement presented on retry #2's bundle: identical paramsHash (NC-2.7), different grant. Only the grant reference can separate retries, and it does.

vectors.name: reject-grant-ref-mismatch
vectors.description: §9.4 — executionGrantHash re-pointed at another value; F1 rule-b recomputation refuses.

vectors.name: reject-authorization-ref-mismatch
vectors.description: §9.4 — authorizationReceiptHash names a different authorization than the bundle's receipt.

vectors.name: reject-allowed-receipt-wrong-verdict
vectors.description: R-8's concern in this package: the hash-bound receipt attests EXECUTED, not ALLOWED — cryptographically bound, semantically contradictory. Its OWN code (see the generator header).

vectors.name: reject-envelope-hash-mismatch
vectors.description: R-23(i) — a supplied holdEnvelope whose refHash != grant.holdEnvelopeHash; otherwise R-23 reads mode off an envelope nothing binds.

vectors.name: reject-hmac-params-hash
vectors.description: §7 step 1 (offline) — a keyed paramsHash is not third-party checkable: boundsStatus UNCHECKED, no positive, offline tier.

vectors.name: reject-hmac-params-derivation
vectors.description: REVISION 3 — the keyed form blocks the D7 DERIVATION too, not only bounds: a real on-chain settlement is supplied and the result is still SETTLEMENT_BOUNDS_UNCHECKABLE, never a positive.

vectors.name: reject-no-params-preimage
vectors.description: §7 step 1 — no preimage supplied: the bounds were never compared, so no positive is reachable.

vectors.name: reject-params-preimage-hash-mismatch
vectors.description: §7 step 1 — a preimage whose SHA-256 does not equal action.paramsHash: not one field is read from it.

vectors.name: reject-params-preimage-extra-member
vectors.description: R-HASH-2(2) — a hash-matching preimage carrying an unknown member is a refusal, not a tolerance.

vectors.name: reject-params-preimage-noncanonical-whitespace
vectors.description: R-HASH-2 canonical form (whitespace) — the bytes parse to the six approved members and hash to their own receipt's paramsHash, but they are not the JCS encoding of that document. Accepting them lets one set of parameters carry more than one valid paramsHash.

vectors.name: reject-params-preimage-noncanonical-member-order
vectors.description: R-HASH-2 canonical form (member-order) — the bytes parse to the six approved members and hash to their own receipt's paramsHash, but they are not the JCS encoding of that document. Accepting them lets one set of parameters carry more than one valid paramsHash.

vectors.name: reject-params-preimage-noncanonical-escaping
vectors.description: R-HASH-2 canonical form (escaping) — the bytes parse to the six approved members and hash to their own receipt's paramsHash, but they are not the JCS encoding of that document. Accepting them lets one set of parameters carry more than one valid paramsHash.

vectors.name: reject-chainid-from-artifact
vectors.description: REVISION 3 — a UNIFORMLY testnet-consistent artifact + chain facts (what an implementation lifting derivation inputs from the artifact would accept) against a preimage that says mainnet: the verified preimage wins.

vectors.name: reject-unsafe-chainid
vectors.description: A chainId the schema grammar admits (19 digits max) but the derivation refuses (> 2^53-1, non-safe integer): fail-closed by arithmetic, and this vector is what makes that documented claim measured. No silent misderivation band exists — any inexact Number() rounding lands on a non-safe integer.

vectors.name: reject-testnet-as-mainnet
vectors.description: B1 — testnet coordinates presented for a mainnet mandate.

vectors.name: reject-counterfeit-asset
vectors.description: §9.6 / B2 — a look-alike EIP-3009 token emits a genuine AuthorizationUsed(payer, correlation); the asset bound against the verified preimage is what refuses it.

vectors.name: reject-wrong-payer
vectors.description: B3 — a third party burned an equal nonce from its own address; (authorizer, nonce) is the namespace.

vectors.name: reject-wrong-payee
vectors.description: B4 — the observer reports a payee the mandate never approved; caught offline.

vectors.name: reject-amount-over-bound
vectors.description: B5 — reported amount above maxAmountMinorUnits.

vectors.name: reject-zero-value-burn
vectors.description: §9.6 / B6 — a zero-value transferWithAuthorization consumes the nonce for free; 0 <= max means B5 alone cannot catch it.

vectors.name: reject-status-inconsistent
vectors.description: R-9 — NOT_OBSERVED with a non-null txHash is a self-contradicting artifact.

vectors.name: reject-settled-missing-amount
vectors.description: R-10 — SETTLED with amount null: 'settled, amount unknown' must never be accepted as a positive.

vectors.name: reject-amount-over-uint256
vectors.description: R-11b — a 78-digit amount the schema regex admits and no EIP-3009 contract could emit.

vectors.name: reject-asset-network-mismatch
vectors.description: R-11c — asset on eip155:8453 under network eip155:84532; the two patterns do not enforce agreement.

vectors.name: reject-settled-before-grant
vectors.description: R-13 — a settlement that predates its authorization is incoherent.

vectors.name: reject-unknown-rail-family
vectors.description: R-6 — an unknown rail family fails CLOSED: different rails bind the correlation with different strength.

vectors.name: reject-observer-identity-split
vectors.description: The document names one observer and is signed by another; without this the R-16 cap is dodged by naming a different kid.

vectors.name: reject-malformed-base64
vectors.description: R-RAIL-2(i) — OUR OWN artifact malformed: bytes that fail the strict base64 round-trip. Buffer.from(s, 'base64') never throws, so the round-trip is the check.

vectors.name: reject-impossible-settledAt
vectors.description: settledAt names a day that does not exist (2026-07-44). Date.UTC used to NORMALIZE it to Aug 13 — the base fixture's real block time — and the artifact earned the positive; the strict calendar parser refuses the string outright.

vectors.name: reject-substituted-payment
vectors.description: §9.1 — authorizationState false, zero logs, artifact claims SETTLED: a different payment carries different bytes.

vectors.name: reject-substituted-txhash
vectors.description: §9.1(2) / R-20 — the coordinates resolve tx X; the artifact reports tx Y. A facilitator can settle a different payment and return its txHash; a reported value can only contradict, never establish.

vectors.name: reject-state-false-with-log
vectors.description: ONE SUCCESS AuthorizationUsed log with authorizationState false: EIP-3009 sets the state bit when it emits the log, so this record describes an impossible chain state and fails CLOSED. Knockout: skip the conjunction -> this vector earns the positive.

vectors.name: reject-log-wrong-nonce
vectors.description: The used log carries a DIFFERENT on-chain nonce than the recomputed correlation: a log lifted from an unrelated transaction is a different payment, and without the binding field the record could not even express the difference.

vectors.name: reject-log-wrong-authorizer
vectors.description: The used log's authorizer is not the approved payer: EIP-3009 uniqueness is per (authorizer, nonce), so a third party's log for an equal nonce is a different fact.

vectors.name: reject-transfer-foreign-tx
vectors.description: The recovered transfer names a DIFFERENT transaction than the AuthorizationUsed log: the same-block decoy in another tx satisfies every value bound while the settling transaction paid someone else. Knockout: drop the txHash binding -> GREEN.

vectors.name: reject-settledAt-contradicts-blocktime
vectors.description: R-20's settledAt arm — a fabricated in-window settledAt contradicting the real blockTimestamp as INSTANTS; nothing else catches this fabrication, and before this vector no test executed the arm.

vectors.name: reject-cancel-foreign-nonce
vectors.description: A SUCCESSFUL AuthorizationCanceled log carrying a FOREIGN (payer, nonce): before the binding fields it burned THIS correlation on an unrelated cancel (SETTLEMENT_CORRELATION_BURNED). The schema now requires the pair on canceled logs and the reconciler asserts it against the recomputed correlation, so a cancel for a different authorization contradicts the record rather than burning ours. Knockout: drop the canceled-log nonce binding -> this vector burns.

vectors.name: reject-year-0099-not-1999
vectors.description: Date.UTC(year,...) maps years 0000-0099 onto 1900-1999, so a settledAt of 0099-08-13 and a resolved blockTimestamp of 1999-08-13 (instants 1900 years apart) both parsed to 1999 and the R-20 corroboration passed -> a positive. The grant's OWN window is in year 0099, so the ordering arm does not mask it. parseInstant now sets the true year explicitly, so the two disagree as instants.

vectors.name: reject-two-logs
vectors.description: R-18 — two AuthorizationUsed entries for one single-use (payer, nonce): the caller's record is wrong, or the coordinates are.

vectors.name: reject-reverted-tx
vectors.description: R-19b — txStatus REVERTED: a reverted transaction changes no state; a log read that ignores status is the naive check.

vectors.name: reject-decoy-transfer-log
vectors.description: R-19(b) — a batched transaction carrying a worthless-token Transfer payer->approved-payee for a compliant amount; log.address == asset refuses it. Knockout: drop the address constraint -> GREEN and the money went to mallory.

vectors.name: reject-two-transfer-logs
vectors.description: R-19(b) uniqueness — two qualifying transfers, presented the only way the record can carry them; the record is refused, the verifier never picks (see the generator header).

vectors.name: reject-chainfacts-from-bundle
vectors.description: R-17b — the fact record travelled inside the evidence bundle, i.e. was supplied by the party being judged.

vectors.name: reject-insufficient-depth
vectors.description: R-17c — a one-block-deep settlement against minConfirmations 12: never RECONFIRMED at unknown depth.

vectors.name: reject-no-min-confirmations
vectors.description: R-17c — the caller supplied no depth policy; no upgrade.

vectors.name: reject-settledAt-format-variance
vectors.description: R-20 regression pin (a non-rejection): '…04.000Z' vs '…04Z' are the SAME instant and different strings. Knockout: compare as strings -> this vector goes RED with a manufactured rejection.

vectors.name: reject-raw-mode-hold
vectors.description: R-23 — hand-assembled RAW envelope under a grant that binds it, everything else green INCLUDING the chain. The cap sets chainStatus AND code AND warning together (R-22).

vectors.name: reject-holdresolution-unenforced
vectors.description: R-23b — the gate-signed resolution attests HUMAN_ACK_UNENFORCED: strictly stronger than reading mode, because it is what the gate itself said.

vectors.name: control-transfer-log-route
vectors.description: R-19 route (b) with all three constraints met: address == asset, from == payer, exactly one.

vectors.name: control-rail-receipt-absent
vectors.description: R-RAIL-1 — absence must not block the positive.

vectors.name: control-rail-receipt-garbage
vectors.description: R-RAIL-2(ii) — the counterparty has no denial-of-verification switch: unparseable bytes are a warning, never a rejection.

vectors.name: control-rail-receipt-wrong-signer
vectors.description: R-RAIL-3 — signed by an address that is not payTo; we never checked, and the verdict is unmoved.

vectors.name: control-rail-receipt-hash-only
vectors.description: R-RAIL-5 — the HASH_ONLY branch records a commitment and claims nothing about the withheld bytes.

vectors.name: control-no-chainfacts-offline
vectors.description: R-22 — a perfect artifact with no chain access earns NO upgrade: the OFFLINE tier's best result.

vectors.name: control-same-key-observer
vectors.description: R-16 — the observer kid IS the execution signer's kid, WITH green chain facts: capped, warned, never positive.

vectors.name: control-alias-kid-observer
vectors.description: The grant signer's PUBLIC KEY registered under a SECOND kid holding the observer role; the artifact is signed with that key under the alias. This is BOTH the alias evasion of a kid-string R-16 cap AND the legitimate dual-role configuration (one key, both roles, two kids): the byte-level cap catches both. Knockout: revert the cap to kid-string equality -> this vector earns the positive.

vectors.name: control-not-observed
vectors.description: §3.2's three-value status: 'we did not look' is NOT 'it did not happen' — and no code containing DID_NOT or FAILED exists to return.

vectors.name: control-not-settled-at-observation
vectors.description: The third status value finally has somewhere to surface — distinguishable from the no-chain-facts case.

vectors.name: control-correlation-cancelled
vectors.description: R-21b — authorizationState true, zero AuthorizationUsed, one AuthorizationCanceled: burned without payment, terminal, NOT 'not yet'. Knockout: drop the cancel branch -> UNRECONFIRMED forever.

vectors.name: control-reverted-cancel-ignored
vectors.description: A REVERTED cancelAuthorization entry alongside the genuine settlement: a reverted transaction changed no state, so it neither contradicts the settlement nor counts toward a burn. A post-settlement cancel reverting with 'authorization already used' is a real, observable chain event; flipping an honest settlement on it manufactures a rejection from an honest state.

vectors.name: control-reverted-cancel-foreign-nonce
vectors.description: The precedence rule, pinned from the other side: a REVERTED cancelAuthorization entry carrying a FOREIGN (payer, nonce) alongside the genuine settlement. Its sibling control proves a reverted cancel with OUR coordinates is ignored; this one proves the coordinate binding is checked FIRST and on EVERY canceled entry, because a record assembled for one authorization that carries another authorization's log is a broken record whatever that log's transaction did. Knockout: apply the binding only to SUCCESS cancels -> a record naming somebody else's authorization earns the positive.

vectors.name: control-settled-after-grant-expiry
vectors.description: R-13 SHOULD — facilitator delay pushed settlement past the grant window; the single-use burn already happened at dispatch. A warning, not a rejection — named so nobody tightens it into a false negative.
